Handing off the weekly stock-variance report for warehouses B and D. Source: the Aug 3-9 ledger export (ledger_aug03_09.csv) and the on-hand snapshot taken Sunday night. Flag every SKU where on-hand differs from the ledger by more than 2 units. Leave out returns-in-transit; they are tracked separately. Output a table with columns sku, warehouse, ledger_qty, onhand_qty, delta, sorted by absolute delta, largest first. Due before the 16:00 sync.

Before I start: does 'more than 2 units' mean an absolute difference strictly greater than 2, or the difference after the 14 cycle-count adjustments posted on Aug 8? Those adjustments move 9 SKUs across the threshold either way, so the answer changes the list.

Strictly greater than 2 in absolute value, measured after the Aug 8 adjustments. If a SKU appears on two ledger lines, sum them first. SKUs sitting at exactly 2 are excluded. You don't need to check back with me on edge cases like that; use your judgment and note it in the footer.

Spring promo cohort summary: 168 refunds out of 3,200 orders, a refund rate of 6.2%. Mean refund 41.50, total refunded 6,972.00. Median days to refund: 6. Cohort window: Apr 1 to Apr 30.

The refund rate does not match the counts. 168 / 3,200 is 5.25%, not 6.2%. The total does check out (168 x 41.50 = 6,972.00). A rate of 6.2% would need about 198 refunds on 3,200 orders, or a denominator near 2,710. Which one did you use?

My error: I divided by 2,710 shipped orders (3,200 minus 490 cancelled before shipment) but labelled it as the all-orders rate. Corrected: 5.25% of all orders, 6.2% of shipped orders. I have relabelled the second as 'refund rate (shipped orders)' and put both in the summary. The totals and the 6-day median are unchanged.
